thesis: FCX is up ~27% over 60 days largely tracking copper's rally to a fresh all-time high (LME copper set a record this week) driven by tariff-front-running and weak ex-China mine supply -- a macro/commodity-wide move, not a fresh Freeport-specific catalyst. The one company-specific positive, the Grasberg Block Cave mine's phased restart after 2025's mudflow incident, was already guided months ago (targeting 65% capacity by 2H26) and isn't new. Today FCX fell roughly 7% intraday as copper retreated from its record high, and Bernstein just cut its price target to $47, well below the current price -- the same tariff-speculation trade that drove the run-up is now unwinding in real time. The evidence is mixed: the dominant driver is sentiment/macro positioning rather than a disclosed Freeport fundamental, and today's sharp reversal shows how quickly that can turn.
invalidation: copper prices stabilize and hold near record levels without a further single-day reversal, and Freeport confirms the Grasberg ramp is on or ahead of the guided 65%-by-2H26 schedule with cost benefits flowing through

thesis: CNQ just reported Q2 2026 earnings (adjusted EPS $1.58 vs. $1.43 est.; revenue $10.6B vs. $9.2B est.) with record quarterly production of ~1.677M boe/d, up 18% YoY -- a confirmed, company-disclosed operating beat, not a rumor or a technical pattern. The stock also benefits from Brent crude pushing toward $100/bbl on Middle East (Israel-Iran) supply risk, but the production growth and earnings beat are Canadian Natural's own execution, not merely a commodity pass-through. The main counter-case is that today's fresh 52-week high partly reflects the same geopolitical oil-price spike that could reverse if tensions ease -- but the record 1.677M boe/d output and the EPS beat have already happened and don't unwind even if Brent gives back some of its recent gain; CNQ's low-cost oil sands operations stay profitable well below current oil prices, so a moderate pullback in crude doesn't invalidate the earnings-driven re-rating.
invalidation: Q3 production or costs miss guidance, or oil prices fall sharply (e.g., Brent back under roughly $75) in a way that pressures realized pricing well below the levels supporting the Q2 beat

thesis: Adobe reported Q3 FY26 results today: revenue $6.76B (vs. $6.70B est., +13% YoY) and non-GAAP EPS $6.13 (vs. $6.09 est.), with full-year guidance raised -- a real, already-disclosed beat, not a rumor or forecast. But the beat was narrow (about 1% on both lines) and shares fell initially in the after-hours session on continued investor concern about Adobe's ability to monetize AI competitively, even with guidance raised. Adobe simultaneously named a new CEO (Anil Chakravarthy, effective Dec 1), a planned, board-endorsed internal succession first flagged back in March rather than a forced departure -- not a red flag on its own, but it layers transition uncertainty onto a stock already down about 48% over the past year on AI-competition concerns. The 60-day pre-earnings run-up (+10.5%) had already priced in optimism, so today's soft initial reaction to an in-line-ish beat reads as the market wanting more, not confirmation of a durable turn -- mixed evidence, not a clean net read.
invalidation: the post-earnings reaction stabilizes or turns positive over the next session or two and management's AI-ARR commentary quiets monetization concerns, alongside a clean CEO transition with no guidance disruption

thesis: KVUE's 3.2x volume spike today isn't a fresh Kenvue-specific catalyst -- it's merger-arbitrage trading around the pending, already-approved Kimberly-Clark acquisition (shareholder votes and the HSR antitrust waiting period cleared back in Jan/Feb 2026, deal targeted to close Q4 2026). The stock is down about 2.7% today, tracking the fixed 0.14625-KMB-shares-plus-$3.50-cash exchange terms and Kimberly-Clark's own share price rather than any new Kenvue operating news. Coverage flags real remaining risk in the deal itself: about $1.9B in targeted cost synergies (roughly 15% of COGS+opex, called high by analysts), integration/restructuring execution risk, and still-open foreign regulatory approvals -- a mechanical, deal-completion-risk trade rather than a fundamental read on Kenvue's underlying business.
invalidation: a fresh, Kenvue-specific catalyst emerges independent of the merger, or the deal breaks and KVUE reverts to trading on its own standalone fundamentals, changing the mechanical merger-arb read
